# Slack

`slack` reads the Slack workspace of whoever connected it on nanou.ai → Connectors → Slack, as them. Output is JSON. When several people connected it, add `--owner <first name>`; use the asker's own unless they name someone else. `slack whoami` says what their token can do (`works`, `missing`).

Read:

- `slack channels --search dev`: channels and DMs they are in
- `slack history --channel '#general' --since 2026-10-14 --limit 30`
- `slack thread --channel '#general' --ts 1729000000.123456`
- `slack search 'from:@ana in:#dev after:2026-10-01' --limit 20`
- `slack users --search ana`

Change (each one gets an approval card; run it as is, without `--readonly`):

- `slack send --channel '#dev' --text "..." [--thread-ts <ts>]` (also `--channel @handle` or an email for a DM)
- `slack react --channel '#dev' --ts <ts> --emoji eyes`

Write as the person would on Slack: short and plain. Reply in the thread (`--thread-ts`) when answering a threaded message.

## Rules

- If `slack` says it isn't connected, send them to nanou.ai → Connectors → Slack. Never ask for a token in chat.
- Never touch `~/.config/connectors/slack` (the tokens live there; it's blocked).
- Work content may be confidential: summarize rather than paste long threads, and don't copy it into family lists or notes unless they ask.
